<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Verdict | Confirmed |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | Medium |
| Task type | Workflow correctness and recovery |

### What Was Claimed

After GitHub accepts a merge, post-merge artifact, issue-close, cleanup, terminal-artifact, or completion work can fail before the `workflow:merged` issue projection is written. The issue can therefore retain `workflow:awaiting-merge` despite a durable merge.

### What We Found

The frozen staging source has two merge paths: orchestrated parent-node integration in `src/workflows/work-on.ts` and direct finalization in the same file. Both perform the merge API call before their durable merge records and downstream post-merge work. The merged label is not treated as the first post-merge barrier, and the orchestrated path additionally swallows the immediate projection failure. Projection reconciliation primarily follows the latest node or terminal run state, so a failure after a successful merge can leave an active run projected as awaiting merge with no later retry.

The direct path currently projects `workflow:merged` before review-completion artifacts, but only after merge effect and phase persistence. The orchestrated path projects before review-completion artifacts but after the merge effect and also has a later generic projection. Both paths need one invariant: successful merge must attempt the merged projection before any subsequent merge bookkeeping or post-merge work, and durable merge evidence must cause reconciliation to retry the merged projection even if later work is incomplete.

### Root Cause

Merge completion and its issue-label projection are separate external effects with no ordering barrier. The implementation allows durable/post-merge operations to run before the merged projection, and reconciliation does not universally recognize a completed merge node/phase as sufficient evidence to restore the merged label.

### Affected Files

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Merge ordering, durable merge completion, and projection reconciliation |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Focused regression coverage for merge projection ordering and durable-merge recovery |

### Evidence

- `#runParentNode` calls `github.mergePullRequest`, records the merge effect, projects `workflow:merged`, then posts review-completion artifacts and only afterward completes the merge node.
- `#finalize` calls `github.mergePullRequest`, records the merge effect and `merge` phase completion, then projects `workflow:merged` before later artifacts; failures in the earlier sequence can still leave the projection stale.
- `#projectWorkflowStage` retries label writes but reports projection failure without durable projection evidence; the parent merge call also catches that failure.
- `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` immediately handles only terminal merged state; otherwise it derives a stage from the latest node, which can cease to be `merge` once close or cleanup work has begun.

### History Findings

The issue body records the finding from PR #117 / source issue #92 (`workflow-correctness-001`). The current source reflects a partial ordering correction in one path, but lacks a shared ordering barrier and complete durable-merge reconciliation fallback. No unrelated history or product contract change is required.

### Recommendation

Move the merged projection barrier ahead of merge bookkeeping and all post-merge work in both merge paths. Add a small sequencing helper so the ordering is executable and testable, and make projection reconciliation recognize any durable completed merge phase/node—even while close or cleanup remains unfinished—so restart recovery repairs a stale label idempotently.

### Related Issues

- Issue #119 (this remediation)
- Source review finding `workflow-correctness-001` from PR #117
- Source issue #92

### Decomposition Assessment

Single concern: one workflow invariant and its recovery coverage. No decomposition is warranted.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] A successful merge attempts `workflow:merged` before merge bookkeeping and post-merge artifacts in both direct and orchestrated paths.
- [ ] A post-merge failure cannot prevent an already-successful merged projection from having been attempted first.
- [ ] Restart/reconciliation retries `workflow:merged` from durable merge phase/node evidence even when later terminal work is incomplete.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover ordering and durable-merge recognition.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.
